## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag must also read its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, as the project's cli-flags rule requires for every new flag. Without it, CI cannot set exclusions through the environment. No other defects were found in the changed filtering logic or its tests.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option. `collect()` uses it to skip files whose basename matches any pattern, and logs each skipped path. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, collection and end-to-end archive tests.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Take the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — When CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, this flag ignores it, because `default=[]` is hard-coded. That breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". `--exclude` is new, so the rule's exemption for older flags does not cover it. — CI jobs that configure archive options through the environment cannot exclude files and will archive content they meant to skip. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, split on a documented separator such as `os.pathsep` because the flag is repeatable, document the variable in `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment case.
